clue.text: Coward, for example, awfully wary in tricky situation

indicators.note: something done awfully is done badly, so these letters come out jumbled
in tells us one group of letters sits inside another word

blocks.note: a plight is an awkward predicament
the four letters of wary rearranged

explanation.surface: A cowardly person behaves very cautiously when caught in an awkward spot.
explanation.walkthrough: Coward reads as a timid person, but it is Noël Coward, the English dramatist; the jumbled WARY goes inside PLIGHT after its first two letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Noël Coward wrote plays such as Private Lives, so he is an example of a dramatist.

clue.text: Alternative to apple for Adam and Eve, say

indicators.note: say asks us to think of how a word is spoken rather than spelt

blocks.note: the first man and woman are a couple, which is spoken the same as the fruit

explanation.surface: The Eden story with a different fruit offered to the first couple.
explanation.walkthrough: The apple seems to belong to the Garden of Eden, but here it is simply one fruit beside another.
explanation.definitionFit: A pear is another common orchard fruit, a natural substitute for an apple in a fruit bowl.

clue.text: Trouble about British workers forming corporation

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one word wraps round a letter

blocks.note: ado is fuss or bother
standard abbreviation for British
men as in a workforce

explanation.surface: Industrial unrest among British staff over the setting up of a company.
explanation.walkthrough: Corporation looks like a business, but its old jokey sense is a large belly.
explanation.definitionFit: Corporation is a humorous dated word for a pot belly, and the abdomen is the belly region.

clue.text: Wagner's beginning with his masterpiece about old Russian woman dreaming

indicators.note: beginning points to only the opening letter of the word before it

blocks.note: the opening letter of the composer's name
about suggests round, and a round letter is O
standard abbreviation for old
Olga is a typical Russian woman's name; its O is supplied by old
Wagner's great opera cycle is known as The Ring

explanation.surface: A music-lover's reverie on Wagner's greatest work and a Russian woman.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run W, O, O-LGA (OLGA), THE RING: Wagner's masterpiece is his four-opera Ring cycle. The parse of about as O is loose; the pieces still give exactly the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Wool-gathering is idle daydreaming, letting the mind wander as if picking scraps of wool off hedges.

clue.text: Demand from assassins is threat

indicators.note: from says the letters are taken out of the words that follow

blocks.note: runs across the end of assassins, all of is and the start of threat

explanation.surface: Killers issuing a threat as their demand.
explanation.definitionFit: To insist is to demand firmly, both verbs of pressing for something.

clue.text: Accommodation arranged shortly after European comes in

indicators.note: arranged means put into a new order, so the letters are reordered
comes in means a letter enters the middle of another group

blocks.note: the letters of shortly rearranged
standard abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: Lodging gets sorted out soon after a European guest arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: Shortly looks like an adverb meaning soon, but it is the anagram fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: A hostelry is an inn or pub offering rooms, a place providing lodging.

clue.text: Instrument taken back for neighbour

indicators.note: taken back suggests going in the opposite direction, so the word is read from right to left

blocks.note: a large brass instrument

explanation.surface: Someone returns a borrowed instrument to the person next door.
explanation.definitionFit: To abut is to lie next to and touch, which is what neighbouring properties do.

clue.text: Romeo tucked into one kind of chicken or another

indicators.note: tucked into means placed inside, so one letter goes within a word

blocks.note: Romeo is R in the NATO phonetic alphabet
a boiler is an older bird fit only for boiling

explanation.surface: A young lover sitting down to a chicken dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is just 'another', meaning another kind of chicken: a broiler is a young bird reared for grilling.
explanation.definitionFit: Another kind of chicken: a broiler is a young bird bred for roasting or grilling, unlike a boiler.

clue.text: Heaney rhymes very little

blocks.note: surface reading: the poet Seamus Heaney writing verse
setter's reading: the answer is two words that each rhyme with the poet's surname

explanation.surface: A critic sniffs that Seamus Heaney's verse amounts to very little.
explanation.walkthrough: Seamus Heaney was an Irish Nobel-winning poet; both halves of the answer rhyme with his name.
explanation.definitionFit: Teeny-weeny is a childish reduplicated word for tiny, i.e. extremely small.

clue.text: Taxing a couple in middle of rural America

indicators.note: middle of points to the central letter of the word after it
in says one piece goes inside the letters around it

blocks.note: taken as written
the third of the five letters
a duo is a pair
standard abbreviation for the United States

explanation.surface: A pair living out in the American countryside find life hard.
explanation.walkthrough: Rural America is surface scenery; middle of rural takes its central letter, and the pair sits inside the letters around it.
explanation.definitionFit: Taxing and arduous both describe a task that is demanding and strenuous.

clue.text: Imagine leading when in second place

blocks.note: standard abbreviation for second
a team that is up is ahead
to pose something is to place or set it in position

explanation.surface: A paradox: thinking you are ahead while actually lying second.
explanation.walkthrough: Pose is used in its sense of to set in position; the leading word goes second, straight after the abbreviation for second.
explanation.definitionFit: To suppose is to assume or picture something as being so, much as one may imagine it.

clue.text: Capital removed from country, betting on pound and yen with great care

indicators.note: capital removed means the opening letter of the country's name is dropped

blocks.note: the European country
staking money is betting it
L for libra, the pound sterling
Y is the symbol for the Japanese yen

explanation.surface: Taking money abroad to gamble on currencies, done very carefully.
explanation.walkthrough: Capital looks like money, which fits the currency surface; here it means a capital, or first, letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Painstakingly means with meticulous, thorough attention, i.e. taking pains over every detail.

clue.text: Wise men in a row, holding trial, initially, in appropriate way

indicators.note: initially takes just the first letter of the word before it
holding means gripping something inside, so a letter goes within

blocks.note: the Magi were the wise men of the Nativity
one after another in a series
the opening letter

explanation.surface: The three wise men lined up in order, judging a case as it should be done.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on 'appropriate': the way of a magistrate, fitting for one who holds trials.
explanation.definitionFit: Magisterially means with the authority of a magistrate, the manner fitting a master or judge.

clue.text: Correct perspective formed by 1 Across and Down

blocks.note: correct means right
an angle is a point of view

explanation.surface: Two crossing entries giving the proper outlook on things.
explanation.walkthrough: 1 Across runs right from the top-left square and 1 Down runs downward from it, so they meet at ninety degrees.
explanation.definitionFit: Across and down entries starting from one corner square meet perpendicularly, making a ninety-degree corner.

clue.text: Local scoffed, not needing to be taught

blocks.note: a local is one's neighbourhood pub
scoffed means ate greedily

explanation.surface: Someone wolfs down food at the pub without any lessons in how.
explanation.walkthrough: In British usage 'the local' is the nearby pub, here an inn.
explanation.definitionFit: Innate qualities are inborn, present from birth rather than learned.

clue.text: Protect page in front of book

blocks.note: standard abbreviation for page
to book a table is to reserve it

explanation.surface: Guarding the opening page of a volume.
explanation.walkthrough: Book looks like a noun, but it is the verb meaning to reserve.
explanation.definitionFit: To preserve something is to keep it safe from harm or decay.

clue.text: County players collectively disheartened

blocks.note: Down is a county of Northern Ireland
the cast is the whole company of actors

explanation.surface: A county sports team, the whole side, feeling low after defeat.
explanation.walkthrough: County Down is in Northern Ireland; players means actors here, not sportsmen.
explanation.definitionFit: Downcast describes someone low in spirits, dejected and discouraged.

clue.text: Before fight, gym equipment's put in trailer

blocks.note: the vaulting horse in a gym
to box is to fight with fists

explanation.surface: Gym kit gets loaded into a trailer before a boxing bout.
explanation.walkthrough: Before fight means the gym piece comes ahead of the fighting word.
explanation.definitionFit: A horsebox is a vehicle or towed trailer for transporting horses.

clue.text: Company car ahead overturned over wild animal

indicators.note: overturned means turned upside down, so in a down entry the word runs backwards

blocks.note: taken as written
standard abbreviation for company
on means over, as in a lid on a box

explanation.surface: A company vehicle flips over after hitting a wild animal.
explanation.walkthrough: The overturned car goes ahead of the company abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: A raccoon is a masked North American mammal that lives in the wild.

clue.text: Come to pass, maybe, in the Yorkshire Dales

blocks.note: first meaning: to occur
second meaning: northern English dialect for perhaps

explanation.walkthrough: The Yorkshire Dales are hill country in northern England, where 'happen' is used as an adverb meaning perhaps.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that happen occur, and in Yorkshire speech 'happen' is also a word for possibly.

clue.text: Paint some farm workers put on front of tractor

indicators.note: front of means only the first letter of the following word is used

blocks.note: farm hands who look after the pigs
the opening letter

explanation.surface: A farm instruction to some hands to paint the front of the tractor.
explanation.definitionFit: Pigment is colouring matter, and paint is likewise colour applied to a surface.

clue.text: Black king, repeatedly, of African people

blocks.note: B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils
ER, Edward Rex, is a king
the same two pieces written a second time

explanation.surface: A dark-skinned monarch who keeps recurring in an African tribe's history.
explanation.walkthrough: Repeatedly tells us to write the pair of pieces twice.
explanation.definitionFit: The Berbers are the indigenous peoples of North Africa.

clue.text: Job for someone with lots to offer

definitions.text: Job for someone with lots to offer

blocks.note: surface reading: a generous or talented person
setter's reading: lots are the numbered items put up at a sale by bidding

explanation.walkthrough: Lots to offer sounds like plenty of talent; read literally, the lots are sale items offered to bidders.
explanation.definitionFit: Running sales by bidding, offering lot after lot, is the trade of the person with the gavel.

clue.text: Edge from side of bat followed by another

indicators.note: side of means a letter at one edge of the word, here its first

blocks.note: the opening letter
another word for edge, the definition

explanation.surface: A cricket ball flies off the edge of the bat, then off another.
explanation.walkthrough: Another means a second word meaning edge.
explanation.definitionFit: The brim of a cup or hat is its edge or rim.

clue.text: Female from part of US or USSR formerly

definitions.text: part of US or USSR formerly

blocks.note: first meaning: a woman's name

blocks.clueFragment: part of US or USSR formerly
blocks.note: second meaning: an American state and also a former Soviet republic

explanation.surface: A woman who hails from America or the old Soviet Union.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a girl's name, a southern American state, and a Caucasus country once a Soviet republic.

clue.text: Following error, produce something really frightful

blocks.note: a bug is a fault in software
to bear fruit is to produce it

explanation.surface: A mistake leads to the creation of something truly dreadful.
explanation.walkthrough: Following error puts the error word first.
explanation.definitionFit: A bugbear was originally an imaginary goblin used to frighten children, something to be dreaded.

clue.text: It could erupt in Vietnam or Estonia, oddly

indicators.note: oddly means taking the letters in the odd-numbered positions

blocks.note: first, third, fifth and seventh letters

explanation.surface: A volcano that might blow in southeast Asia or the Baltic.
explanation.walkthrough: A bonus: the answer also sits inside Vietnam, so the clue gives it two ways.
explanation.definitionFit: Etna is the active volcano on Sicily, liable to erupt at any time.

clue.text: Lots of heavenly bodies, something Hollywood relied on

blocks.note: first meaning: a group of stars bound together
second meaning: studios' practice of building films around contracted stars

explanation.walkthrough: Heavenly bodies hints at glamorous film stars too, linking the two senses.
explanation.definitionFit: Astronomers use it for a gravitationally bound group of stars, and the old studios used it for promoting contracted actors.
